status: Scoring weights are Mysoft's judgement. Every capability statement in reasons, gaps and the fit profile is checked against the sources in 'sources'.

questions.text: What does your business mainly do?
questions.helper: Pick the one that drives most of your revenue.

reason.x3: You make products, and Sage X3 is built for manufacturers, covering production, inventory, sales and finance in one system.
You distribute or wholesale, and Sage X3 includes advanced warehouse management alongside finance.

reason.intacct: You run a professional services business, and Sage Intacct includes project accounting.
You sell software or subscriptions, and Sage Intacct includes subscription billing and revenue recognition.
You are a non-profit, and Sage Intacct can report on funds, grants and donations.
You are in financial services, where the main need is finance and reporting rather than stock or production.

questions.text: How much stock do you manage?
questions.helper: Think about physical goods you buy, hold or make.

reason.intacct: You hold no stock, so you do not need supply chain or production features.
Your stock is simple, and Sage Intacct includes inventory management across multiple locations.

options.label: Several warehouses, lot or serial tracking

reason.x3: You run several warehouses or need lot and serial tracking, both of which Sage X3 provides.

options.label: We manufacture: bills of materials, routings or recipes

reason.x3: You manufacture, and Sage X3 supports both process and discrete manufacturing.

questions.text: How many legal entities do you report on?
questions.helper: Include subsidiaries, overseas companies and any entities you consolidate.

reason.intacct: You report on several entities, and Sage Intacct automates multi-entity consolidation.
You consolidate many entities, and Sage Intacct consolidates entities across currencies automatically.
reason.x3: You run many entities, and Sage X3 provides multi-site, multi-currency and multi-country management.

reason.intacct: You consolidate many entities, and Sage Intacct consolidates entities across currencies automatically.
reason.x3: You run many entities, and Sage X3 provides multi-site, multi-currency and multi-country management.

questions.helper: Count countries where you have a legal entity or file tax returns.

options.label: UK and a few other countries

reason.intacct: You operate in a few countries, and Sage Intacct consolidates across currencies.

reason.x3: You operate in six or more countries, and Sage X3 has built-in support for multiple countries, currencies and legislations.

reason.intacct: You bill subscriptions or recurring contracts, and Sage Intacct includes subscription billing and revenue recognition.
You bill projects or time, and Sage Intacct includes project accounting.
You manage grants or restricted funds, and Sage Intacct can report on funds and grants.

reason.x3: You process high order volumes, and Sage X3 covers sales, inventory and warehousing in one system.

questions.text: How do you want to run the system?
questions.helper: On-premise includes private hosting you control.

reason.intacct: You want cloud software, and Sage Intacct is multi-tenant cloud software updated by Sage.

options.label: We need on-premise or private hosting

reason.x3: You are replacing an older ERP, and Sage X3 covers finance, supply chain and production.

questions.text: When do you need a new system live?
questions.helper: Your target go-live date, not when you start looking.

questions.text: Who will support the system internally?
questions.helper: The person or team who will own it after go-live.

questions.text: Is any of these central to how you operate?

options.label: Store-based retail with point of sale
Core banking or insurance policy administration

hardRules.reason: Sage Intacct is cloud-only software with no on-premise option, while Sage X3 can run as SaaS, in a private cloud or on-premise.
You manufacture with bills of materials, routings or recipes, and Sage X3 supports both process and discrete manufacturing.

constraint.issue: At this scale, include at least one tier-one ERP in your shortlist so the comparison is complete.
constraint.action: Ask each supplier for reference customers of your size and country spread.

gaps.issue: Manufacturing on Sage Intacct relies on Sage Distribution and Manufacturing Operations, which Sage describes as for discrete manufacturers, or on a marketplace add-on.
gaps.action: Check UK availability and whether your processes are discrete or process-based, or compare with Sage X3.

gaps.issue: Advanced warehousing on Sage Intacct uses warehouse technology partners listed on the Sage Intacct Marketplace.
gaps.action: Shortlist a warehouse partner early and include it in the scope.

gaps.issue: Confirm local tax, statutory reporting and language support for each country.
gaps.action: Ask each supplier which countries they have delivered in.

gaps.issue: Mysoft publishes its Sage X3 delivery options as 80 service days over six calendar months (Kickstart, which excludes manufacturing) up to 140 service days over twelve months.
gaps.action: Check whether your go-live date allows for the scope you need.

gaps.issue: Decide early how much history to migrate; it affects cost and timeline.
gaps.action: Agree a migration policy before you ask for quotes.

gaps.issue: With no dedicated internal owner, you will rely on your partner after go-live.
gaps.action: Budget for partner support from day one.

gaps.issue: Waiting has a cost in finance team time.
gaps.action: Put a number on it before deciding to wait.

gaps.issue: Mysoft describes Sage Intacct as giving non-profits visibility over funds, grants and donations.
gaps.action: Map your funds and grants early in the design.

gaps.issue: This selector does not assess construction-specific requirements such as contract and job costing.
gaps.action: Ask each supplier to demonstrate your contract processes with your own data.

questionsToAsk: How many implementations like ours have you delivered in the last two years, and can we speak to two of those customers?
What is fixed in your proposal, and what would cause the cost or timeline to change?
Who will actually work on our project, and what is their experience?
How will you migrate our data, and how much history do you recommend bringing across?
What does support look like in the first 90 days after go-live, and after that?

intacct.headline: Sage Intacct is the stronger fit
intacct.ctaLabel: Talk to Mysoft about Sage Intacct
defaultReasons: Sage Intacct automates multi-entity consolidation across currencies.
Sage Intacct includes subscription billing, revenue recognition and project accounting.
Sage Intacct is multi-tenant cloud software, updated by Sage.

x3.headline: Sage X3 is the stronger fit
x3.ctaLabel: Talk to Mysoft about Sage X3
defaultReasons: Sage X3 manages finance, supply chain and production in one system.
Sage X3 includes advanced warehouse management and lot and serial traceability.
Sage X3 can run as SaaS, in a private cloud or on-premise.

both.headline: Both Sage Intacct and Sage X3 could work
both.ctaLabel: Talk to Mysoft about both options
both.summary: Your answers do not clearly favour one product. That usually means light stock and a finance-led brief.
tipIt: If stock, warehousing or production will matter more over the next three years, lean towards Sage X3.
If multi-entity reporting, subscriptions or projects matter more than stock, lean towards Sage Intacct.
If you must run on-premise, Sage X3 is the only option of the two.
Mysoft's published view is that an average Sage Intacct project costs less than an average Sage X3 project because it is faster to deliver.

not-sage.headline: Sage may not be the right lead system for you
not-sage.summary: Store-based retail with point of sale, core banking and insurance policy administration are outside what this selector assesses, so it cannot recommend a Sage product with confidence.
consider: Choose the operational system that runs those processes first, then decide how finance will connect to it.
Ask that vendor which finance systems they integrate with in production today.
Consider Sage Intacct as the finance system if you have several entities to consolidate.

too-early.headline: Your current system may be enough for now
too-early.summary: With one entity, one-off invoicing and revenue under £5m, the features that set Sage Intacct and Sage X3 apart, such as multi-entity consolidation, may not pay back yet.
signals: Month-end close regularly takes more than five working days.
You add a second legal entity or start trading overseas.
Reporting depends on spreadsheets that only one person understands.
You start billing subscriptions, projects or grants.
Your auditors raise controls or audit trail issues.
